Scientific disposition

REDUCE, MERGE, AND PAUSE.

The existing evidence is sufficient to reject continued investment in ONLGR at its present scope as a task-content-aware, timing-flexible lease/rebinding mechanism. The defensible residual is much narrower:

a global, task-blind event-rate prior passed through the eligible-exposure link may be a useful finite-budget regularizer relative to a learned per-opportunity RAW probability.

That residual should be separated from the current ONLGR mechanism story and merged into a simpler global-rate or event-shell question. B2 already closes the timing-flexible branch under its frozen decision rule, and the ROAD patch family should remain closed as a valid direct-utility nonpass. No additional same-coordinate, unchanged-checkpoint experiment is sufficiently identifying to justify immediate execution.

This is not a finding that the exposure link has no value. It is a finding that the evidence does not support the broader scientific interpretation for which ONLGR was being considered.

1. Causal trace of the actual B1 object

At each physical tick, the binary mission mode may change and each agent obtains a noisy sensor bit. At a routine boundary, after that tick’s sensor update but before same-tick service, the actor receives task-content coordinates—binding and mismatch information—as well as plan age, lease state, busy state, the realized preceding interval Δt, and eligible exposure e. It does not receive the schedule label, absolute time, callback count, interval history, next interval, or future k.

Conditional on an event, a separate learned mark chooses REFRESH-SAME or REBIND. A non-KEEP action resets age, imposes immediate cost and downtime, and starts the lease; REBIND also flips the binary binding. The resulting post-action state determines same-tick service. Ordinary physical-time SMDP-GAE propagates later service and costs back to the boundary action; there is no special relay credit, association credit, auxiliary reward, or event-specific return.

On RAND-IID-4-16-32, the next interval is drawn only after the current joint action, using a counter keyed by seed, episode, and routine-boundary ordinal. The draw cannot depend on visible history, current state, current action, reward, or previous intervals.

That ordering matters:

visible state and e→u,ρ→marked action→same-tick cost/service and future state→draw next IID k.

Consequently, persistence on IID rules out anticipation of the next cadence. It does not by itself distinguish a useful physical-time link from a good global action-rate prior, exposure-dependent initialization, favorable gradient scaling, or generic shell regularization.

3. Explanation-by-explanation assessment
3.1 Eligible-exposure-link inductive bias
Why it remains plausible

The strongest supporting observation is not the deterministic worst-schedule result; it is the unchanged-checkpoint IID result. ONLGR exceeds RAW by +0.0348194 normalized return, with paired 95% interval [0.0245868, 0.0450520]. Service rises by +0.0351990, while action cost is actually 0.0003796 higher. Thus the result is not merely a bookkeeping gain from paying for fewer actions.

Because the next interval is drawn after the action, this is genuine evidence that the complete ONLGR package can outperform RAW without predicting future cadence from history. It is compatible with an exposure-linked prior that maps the already-realized amount of legal physical exposure into a better current action probability.

The native result is also consistent with coarse-grid regularization. The registered worst-schedule contrast is +0.0405534, with Bonferroni 97.5% interval [0.0329355, 0.0481712], even though the seven-schedule mean contrast is only +0.0065377 and does not pass. ONLGR loses on CONST-4 but wins on CONST-16 and CONST-32, so the effect is a robustness tradeoff rather than uniform dominance.

Why the evidence does not isolate the link

B1 deliberately matches the arms only at one initial point: zero features and e=8 both give u=0.20. The complete initial curves are very different:

ONLGR: u(1)=0.0275, u(4)=0.1056, u(8)=0.20, u(16)=0.36, u(24)=0.488, u(32)=0.5904.

RAW: u(e)=0.20 at every listed exposure.

The corresponding entropy and gradient geometry also differ. This exposure-dependent initialization is explicitly part of the registered finite-budget treatment rather than a controlled-away nuisance.

Therefore B1 identifies a link-plus-optimization-path package. That is a legitimate inductive-bias object, but it does not show that final decisions use exposure in a semantically correct way, nor that the transform conveys task content or predicts future cadence.

The strongest current reading is:

the link may provide a useful global action-rate and gradient prior under this short training budget.

The evidence does not support the stronger reading:

the learned rate combines exposure with current task content to implement a causally correct adaptive renewal mechanism.

3.2 Task content versus timing or tenure sufficiency

TIMING-ONLY retains the ONLGR transform, role, plan age, lease remaining, busy state, cause, preceding interval, and exposure, but zeroes active-binding, own-mismatch, partner-binding, and partner-mismatch coordinates. It therefore removes the content that could say whether the current binding is wrong while preserving the principal timing and shell variables.

On IID,

with 95% interval [-0.0052189, 0.0048762]; the service difference is similarly near zero.

This does more than merely “fail to prove” content use. The upper interval endpoint is far below the registered 0.02 materiality requirement. Within the exact B1 panel, it rules out a registered-material task-content increment. It does not establish literal equality or exclude a much smaller effect.

The observed ONLGR-over-RAW IID advantage is therefore reproducible by a task-content-blind policy. Current binding and mismatch information are not needed to explain it.

B2 then asks the appropriate residual question: does the task-blind rate need to vary with timing, tenure, lease, busy state, and preceding exposure, or is a single learned global λ enough? RATE-FLEX learned a nonconstant mapping in every seed, so the treatment was delivered and did not collapse to the comparator. Nevertheless, its mean advantage was only +0.0009783, with 95% interval [-0.0013578, 0.0033143], far below the 0.02 rule. The frozen branch selects RATE-CONST.

B2 therefore changes the residual explanation materially:

Before B2: a timing/tenure-dependent but content-blind heuristic could explain B1.

After B2: access to timing coordinates remains possible, but a material benefit from learning a timing-dependent λ was not demonstrated.

The leading residual becomes a global λ passed through the live exposure transform, not a rich timing-conditioned rate.

This is not proof that timing never matters. RATE-FLEX learned only a small modulation, and another budget could yield a larger first stage. But such a possibility is a future hypothesis, not support for this treatment.

3.3 Global-rate, shell-regularization, and inaction explanations

The validation-selected state-blind control chose

λ=0.125,ρ=0.5.

Its held-out mean return exceeded ONLGR in every deterministic schedule. The descriptive aggregate contrast was

with ordinary 95% interval [-0.0525154, -0.0207530]; the worst-schedule contrast was also negative, although its interval crossed zero.

This is not a registered superiority test. FIXED-RATE was validation-selected, not learned with matched PPO resources, and its comparison was not a project-facing primary gate. It therefore cannot reverse the B1 ONLGR-versus-RAW estimate.

It is nevertheless highly informative about sufficiency. FIXED-RATE retains:

the same eligible-exposure transform;

the same lease;

the same action costs and downtime;

the same 50/50 mark split;

no task content and no learned timing dependence.

Together with B2, it strongly supports the claim that the important operating point may be a simple state-blind rate plus shell, rather than learned adaptive rebinding.

A pure inaction account is not well supported: on IID, ONLGR pays slightly more action cost than RAW. Its gain is not explained by merely suppressing all interventions. But a broader action-shell explanation survives: the transform may place actions differently across exposure, alter REFRESH/REBIND timing, or regularize the number of scored opportunities without using task content.

The distinction is important. The fixed-rate and B2 global-rate arms still use

u(e)=1−exp(−λe).

They are evidence against ONLGR’s learned content/timing complexity, not evidence against the exposure transform itself.

3.4 Deterministic cadence leakage

The deterministic schedule cells do not expose a schedule label or future interval, and the switch-twin audit verifies that the action, logits, probabilities, and current reward are equal before the next-interval branch.

But the science card correctly notes that this proves only same-boundary nonanticipation. In a constant or alternating schedule, the realized preceding interval and other accumulated state can reveal which cadence process is operating and thereby predict later intervals.

Therefore deterministic cadence inference remains a possible contributor to the native W result. It cannot, however, be the sole explanation for the ONLGR-over-RAW effect, because the IID result persists when every next interval is independently drawn after the action.

What IID eliminates is:

policy advantage from correctly forecasting the next interval from visible history.

What IID does not eliminate is:

an exposure-dependent or globally calibrated action prior that works well on a mixture of independently drawn short and long intervals.

Hence IID persistence supports history-independent usefulness of the package, but it does not isolate task-content-bearing or future-cadence-bearing information in the rate.

3.5 Finite-budget initialization and optimization geometry

This is not a residual technical nuisance; it is one of the leading scientific explanations.

The B1 arms have the same parameter count and receive the same primary inputs, but their link derivatives differ. For ONLGR,

∂g
∂u
	​

=eσ(g)exp[−softplus(g)e],

so exposure directly scales the event-head gradient. RAW has an ordinary sigmoid gradient unrelated to e except through what the network learns from its input coordinates. Combined with the very different initial u(e) curves and only eight batches of training, this can create materially different learning trajectories even though RAW could represent the same finite-state policy after sufficient fitting. The card explicitly classifies this initialization and gradient prior as part of the finite-budget treatment.

B2 removes the initialization mismatch for its own flex-versus-const question: output weights start at zero, both arms have the same initial curve for every feature and exposure, and only actor access to timing features differs.

Its nonpass therefore says that, once the global exposure-linked operating curve is common, eight-update optimization did not derive material value from the additional timing function class. RATE-FLEX’s small but nonzero learned rate variation prevents a “literal collapse” explanation, but weak functional dose and finite-budget geometry remain possible reasons it did not pass.

The combined evidence is most consistent with:

a useful exposure-linked global operating point;

finite-budget optimization advantages relative to RAW;

little demonstrated value from task content or flexible timing modulation.

3.6 Direct-value mismatch and the ROAD result

ROAD is a different scientific object. It has a fixed-t=0 update, a one-second blackout and buffer-clear shell, a road-constrained estimator payload, and four explicit arms: NEVER, SHAM, RAW patch, and ROAD patch. Its inference operates on 128 paired direct-service replicates and separate net-versus-payload gates.

The ROAD package strongly beats nominal RAW, but:

ROAD minus competent NEVER is about -0.0478 on mean service and -0.0463 on tail service, with intervals wholly below zero.

ROAD minus matched SHAM is only +0.00107 on mean and +0.00198 on tail, both far below the registered materiality margins.

Most of the loss relative to NEVER is attributable to the common action shell; the ROAD payload recovers only a small fraction.

This cannot be imported as evidence that the B1 exposure link lacks value. The hosts, treatments, estimators, and decisions differ.

It is, however, a relevant common failure pattern:

A structured treatment can look excellent against a pathological nominal RAW intervention while adding little or no direct value over a competent incumbent or matched shell.

B1 does measure direct return rather than a proxy, so it is not purely a direct-value mismatch. Its limitation is comparator scope: the claim-bearing positive result is against RAW, while the simpler fixed-rate exposure-linked control is descriptively stronger and the task-content/timing refinements do not pass.

4. The unavailable operational partition cannot support a mechanism claim

The equal-time partition probe required every ONLGR and RAW partition in a diagnostic cell to have first-event probability in [0.05,0.95], with the unsplit ONLGR/RAW first-event-probability difference at most 0.05. At least 12 of 16 common cells per seed were required.

No seed had a valid common cell. All 128 cells were excluded because the unsplit activity gap was approximately 0.4117–0.4725, vastly above the guard. Consequently:

MPI and HPI do not exist as registered operational estimands.

Excluded-cell values cannot be averaged or reclassified.

eligible_exposure_link_composite_gate=false is not a negative MPI estimate.

The large unsplit gap is evidence that the arms occupied very different action-probability regimes on the probe; it is not evidence that either arm was more composition-stable.

Repairing the denominator, widening the 0.05 guard, or selecting less-saturated cells after observing this result would be post-result redefinition, not scientific discrimination.

5. Missing controls: claim caps, not reversed estimates

The absent exposure-clamp, yoke, oracle, and degenerate-policy panels do not invalidate or reverse the observed B1 ONLGR-versus-RAW contrasts. They remove specific interpretations:

No clamp: no direct evidence that live variation in e, rather than the trained checkpoint’s broader policy geometry, is needed at evaluation.

No yoke: no action-sequence or dwell-matched sensitivity result.

No oracle: no measured content-access headroom.

No degenerate controls: no clean decomposition against ALWAYS-KEEP, always-refresh, or always-rebind behavior in the retained recovery.

Failed 7M tick cap: no within-registered-resource-cap claim; the statistical comparisons themselves remain the checkpoint-only recovery observations.

These absences cap attribution. They do not turn the positive IID or worst-schedule estimates into null or negative results.

6. Is one more unchanged-checkpoint observation justified?

No.

An immediate unchanged-checkpoint observation cannot cleanly resolve the remaining investment-relevant distinction.

Why the obvious candidates are not sufficient

An IID exposure clamp would change both the event calculation and the endogenous closed-loop action/state distribution. In the registered clamp, it also replaces the actor’s time inputs. Because the checkpoint was trained under the native link, disappearance under clamp would be consistent with direct exposure dependence, distribution shift, action-rate miscalibration, or disruption of learned feature interactions. Persistence would show only that varying live exposure is unnecessary for that frozen policy; it would not separate link-induced training geometry from the learned weights. The science card itself treats clamp disappearance as merely “consistent with,” not proof of, the mechanism.

Evaluating the validation-selected fixed rate on IID would likewise not answer the central question cleanly. It is not a resource-matched learned arm, its scalar was selected for another panel, and B2 already gives a cleaner prospective global-rate-versus-flex comparison.

A repaired partition, activity-matched denominator, alternate threshold, extra seeds, longer training, or retuning would answer a revised post-result question rather than discriminate among the live explanations for the registered objects.

Most importantly, an inductive-bias claim concerns how different links produce different learned checkpoints. Once the checkpoints exist, an evaluation-only remapping cannot disentangle the link’s training effect from the policy it produced without introducing a new calibration or activity confound.

7. Next genuinely prospective revisit condition

The residual question should be revisited only after independent, result-blind evidence establishes both of the following:

a competent global exposure-linked rate and a competent no-action or matched-shell comparator leave material direct-return headroom; and

either equal-physical-time opportunity partitions or two predeclared exposure/tenure strata require materially different event probabilities, rather than merely producing small diagnostic rate variation.

Under that condition, the minimal new object would compare:

one learned global λ,u(e)=1−exp(−λe)

against

one learned global per-opportunity p,u=p,

with no task-content inputs, no flexible timing head, the same fixed mark law, lease, action shell, initialization criterion, training work, post-action IID cadence, and competent direct-value controls. Initial marginal action behavior and any activity matching would have to be fixed prospectively rather than calibrated from outcomes.

That would be a distinct global exposure-link versus global opportunity-probability question. It should not inherit B1 qualification or be described as a continuation of task-content-aware ONLGR. For timing-dependent rates specifically, the repository’s converged B2 revisit condition is similarly prospective: external evidence must first show materially different best rates in two recurrent timing/tenure strata and material headroom over the best global rate.

Final synthesis

Strongest support. B1 supplies a real bounded package result: ONLGR improves the registered seven-schedule worst-case estimator and improves post-action IID return through higher service—not lower action cost—over the matched RAW learner. The IID ordering rules out predictable-next-cadence leakage as the sole explanation.

Strongest contradiction. The same B1 checkpoints show no registered-material increment over task-content-blind TIMING-ONLY; a simple state-blind fixed rate is descriptively stronger across deterministic aggregates; and fresh, treatment-delivered B2 finds only +0.0009783 for timing-flexible over global rate, selecting the global family. ROAD separately demonstrates that a dramatic win over nominal RAW can coexist with no material payload value over a competent incumbent and matched shell.

Remaining alternatives. The live explanations are a global exposure-linked action-rate prior, shell regularization, a favorable initial operating curve and gradient geometry under eight-update PPO, host-specific reward/lease geometry, and weakness of RAW as a finite-budget comparator. Small task-content or timing effects below the registered margins remain possible but are not investment-supporting evidence.

Shared dependencies and common risks. B1 and B2 depend on the same constructed binary two-agent host, fixed lease and mark/action surface, short finite PPO budget, and exposure-linked probability family. Their conclusions may therefore reflect one favorable operating regime rather than a transferable mechanism. ROAD is independent in host and treatment, but exposes the same portfolio risk of over-crediting a treatment because nominal RAW is pathological while a competent null or matched shell is stronger.

Maximum defensible claim.

On the registered constructed two-agent host, under the frozen finite PPO budget and unchanged checkpoints, the complete ONLGR package improved the registered worst-schedule normalized return and post-action IID normalized return and service over a capacity-, input-, action-, lease-, work-, optimizer-, and ordinary-SMDP-GAE-matched RAW learner, while failing to improve the registered seven-schedule mean. The observed IID advantage did not require current binding or mismatch content on the registered materiality margin. A separate fresh B2 experiment did not demonstrate material value from conditioning a task-blind rate on timing and tenure beyond one learned global rate. These findings support at most a host- and budget-specific global exposure-linked regularization hypothesis, not the broader ONLGR mechanism.

Nothing in this record establishes RAW representational impossibility, a literal hazard, causal value of the lease or REBIND, arbitrary or continuous callback periods, variable population size, UAV performance or transfer, safety certification, or general PPO superiority.
